newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-BACHER IN SOUTH AFRICA SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BACHER IN SOUTH AFRICA SQUAD.

text.p: In-form batsman Adam Bacher earned a place in South Africa's 13-man squad announced on Wednesday for the first two home tests against India in December and January.
Bacher, 23-year-old nephew of United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) managing director Ali Bacher, was the only new name in the squad announced by UCBSA president Krish Mackerdhuj.
Fast bowlers Allan Donald and Shaun Pollock return after injury.
The omission of Jonty Rhodes provided the major surprise in a squad in which competition for middle-order batting spots is keen.
Bacher has been the most prolific batsman in South Africa's provincial Supersport Series competition this season, totalling 507 runs in only three matches at an average of 126.75.
He has struck three centuries and one 50 in his three games, including a double century and a century in the same fixture against Griqualand West in Kimberley.
Bacher could fill the number three slot in the batting line-up.

"He's a fine player and he's played well for a couple of seasons and I think we would have been very unwise not to take advantage of a guy who has scored so prolifically," convener of selectors Peter Pollock said.
"The good news usually is that, once a guy gets into form and makes runs, he coninues for the whole season."
Pollock said the inclusion of both Herschelle Gibbs and Jacques Kallis had counted against Rhodes.
"Competition is quite keen in the middle order and Jonty just hasn't made enough runs," Pollock said. "But he's always competitive and I'm sure he'll be back again."

Squad: Hansie Cronje (captain), Gary Kirsten (vice-captain), Andrew Hudson, Herschelle Gibbs, Daryll Cullinan, Jacques Kallis, Brian McMillan, Shaun Pollock, Lance Klusener, Dave Richardson, Allan Donald, Paul Adams, Adam Bacher.
